newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Prize-winning U.S. journalist dies in Bogota crash.
newsitem.headline: Prize-winning U.S. journalist dies in Bogota crash.

text.p: U.S. journalist Thomas Quinn, a former correspondent for Time magazine, was killed and his wife, Zulma, was seriously injured in a road accident early on oSunday in northern Bogota, a foreign press spokesman said.

Quinn, 53, originally from San Diego, came to Colombia 25 years ago to study political science in Bogota's Los Andes University. Most recently he worked as correspondent for Platt's economic news service, according to Alberto Rojas, a family friend and chairman of Colombia's Foreign Press Association.
He said the accident occurred at about 3:30 a.m. EDT (0730 GMT) when the jeep he was driving plunged off a freeway bridge to another road about 60 feet (20 meters) below.
Rojas said Quinn was killed instantly. His wife is in critical condition in Bogota's El Country hospital. The couple have four daughters, one of whom works for Colombian TV news channel QAP.

"Tom was a person who made a great contribution to both national and international journalism. He was well-integrated into Colombian society and because of his work in international journalism was much respected by Colombian government ministers," Rojas said.

Besides his work as a foreign correspondent, Quinn found time to write the script for the TV soap opera Fuego Verde about Colombia's emerald mining industry. He was also planning another TV series about the country's history seen through the eyes of a foreign journalist.
The U.S. correspondent worked as an occasional columnist for Colombia's leading daily El Tiempo and was planing to take over as director of an early morning radio show, according to friends.

Quinn won the Pulitzer prize for a report on emerald mining in Colombia in 1992, according to the TV news NTC. He is also remembered for a controversial interview with kingpins of the then-powerful Cali drug cartel about two years ago.
His funeral is scheduled to take place on Monday in Bogota.
